Remark
[bi-invariant metrics and the Lie exponential]

Source: petersen:page-0242, petersen:page-0243 ↗ def:pet-ch5-exponential-map ↗ thm:pet-ch5-hopf-rinow 1. ch5:5.9.35For a Lie group $G$ with bi-invariant (pseudo-)Riemannian metric: (1) show homomorphisms $\mathbb R\to G$ are precisely the integral curves of left-invariant vector fields through $e$; (2) show geodesics through $e$ are precisely such homomorphisms, so the Lie exponential coincides with the Riemannian exponential at $e$; (3) for a Riemannian (positive-definite) bi-invariant metric, show every $x\in G$ has a square root, using metric completeness; (4) show $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)$ admits no bi-invariant Riemannian metric.
